LESSON: READING ALOUD

Grade: Grade 5
Subject: ARABIC LANGUAGE
Strand: Reading 2.1 Guided Reading: Fluency (2 sessions) • Vocabulary building: Greeting
Topic 2.2: Reading Aloud
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Reading Aloud, part of Reading 2.1 Guided Reading: Fluency (2 sessions) • Vocabulary building: Greeting in Grade 5 ARABIC LANGUAGE.

Key inquiry question: How can you show love to your family members? 2. How does pronunciation affect fluency in reading?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. use simple strategies to read target words in written texts,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading Aloud in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. read short sentences on the family aloud for fluency,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading Aloud in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. appreciate reading strategies for effective communication.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading Aloud in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. use simple strategies to read target words in written texts,

   Reading Aloud helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. read short sentences on the family aloud for fluency,

   Reading Aloud helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. appreciate reading strategies for effective communication.

   Reading Aloud helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

D. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. collaborate with peers to read words aloud in a printed text containing nuun,raa,saad,faa,

2. take-turns to read simple short sentences about immediate family members in a given text,

3. peer review each other’s presentation for constructive feedback,

4. work jointly to read texts containing huwa and hiya,

5. work collaboratively to conduct a reading mini-contest for fluency. 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. collaborate with peers to read words aloud in a printed text containing nuun,raa,saad,faa,
2. take-turns to read simple short sentences about immediate family members in a given text,
3. peer review each other’s presentation for constructive feedback,
4. work jointly to read texts containing huwa and hiya,
5. work collaboratively to conduct a reading mini-contest for fluency. 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Reading Aloud together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Values:
• Responsibility: This is promoted as the learner engages in assigned duties when taking turns to read simple short sentences

about immediate family members.

• Unity: This is enhanced as the learners combine joint efforts when working collaboratively to conduct a reading mini- contest for fluency.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Citizenship: This is addressed as learners accommodate each other as they work in groups to accomplish tasks.

Link to Other Learning Areas:

The learner is able to relate the concept of family to similar concepts as covered in Religious Education.
